name: unnethack
why: A fork of the roguelike NetHack, a deep classic where the variant itself may hold surprises worth an evening.

brief.what_it_is: UnNetHack is a fork of the classic roguelike NetHack, originally based on NetHack 3.4.3. The author describes it as adding more randomness, more levels, more challenges and more fun than vanilla NetHack. You play it like NetHack: you start a character in the terminal and descend the Dungeons of Doom. The project's blog at unnethack.wordpress.com is shared with NetHack-De and mostly covers the UnNetHack project and the annual Junethack tournament. Public online servers exist for US, EU and AU play.
brief.why_it_exists: The README calls UnNetHack 'how NetHack would look today if the DevTeam didn't stop releasing', following a modern open-source development approach.
brief.how_it_works: It is a C source fork of NetHack 3.4.3 with its own level compiler, which the author extended from a patch by Pasi Kallinen and later moved toward Lua level files. A 2020 blog post describes stress-testing that generator by producing one million dungeons each for vanilla and UnNetHack and recording the layouts, which turned up and fixed bugs such as an endless loop in place_random_engraving(). The raw statistics are published.

commands_seen.context: Config option from the 5.2.0 release notes. Setting it gives the same dungeon layout for new games, and the seed is recorded in the dumplog.
Example config line from the 5.2.0 release notes for setting a custom RGB system color on 256-color or 24-bit terminals.

brief.install_notes: The 5.2.0 announcement pointed to SourceForge downloads that included Windows TTY and GUI executables, and said Homebrew for OSX had been updated. Source is on GitHub at UnNetHack/UnNetHack. The README gives no build steps, dependencies or first-run instructions, and I did not follow the separate project page to look for them. Save files from 5.2.0 are not compatible with 5.1.0.
brief.standout: The author published real measurements of the dungeon generator, including how often Fort Ludios and the big room appear across a million generated dungeons, which is unusual for a roguelike fork. The variant also adds a reproducible seed option and new content on top of the 3.4.3 base.
brief.status: Quiet as a release line. The last named release on the blog is UnNetHack 5.2.0, dated 1 January 2019, and the README does not mention newer releases. The blog is still active, with a Junethack 2026 post dated 31 May 2026, but those posts concern the tournament rather than new UnNetHack versions. I could not see the date of the last GitHub commit, so the status is partly unknown.
brief.caveats: No build or install documentation was visible in the README or the homepage. The codebase is based on the 3.4.3 line, not the current NetHack. The 5.2.0 release was not bones or save compatible with 5.1.0. I did not find the license. The blog is mostly tournament posts, so project-specific news is sparse.
quotes: It features more randomness, more levels, more challenges and more fun than vanilla NetHack.
In a nutshell I would describe UnNetHack as how NetHack would look today if the DevTeam didn't stop releasing, following a modern open source project approach of development.
Reproducible dungeon layout. Set OPTIONS=seed:number to get the same dungeon layout for new games.
